beats.label: model request #8
beats.title: Request #8 to the model API
beats.text: The API remembers nothing between calls, so every request resends the system prompt, all 4 tool definitions and all 15 messages so far. The tool definitions alone are about 807 of the 1642 input tokens.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Look up the signed-in customer's account: status (active or cancelled), current plan, its price and features, tenure, and any discount. The customer is identified by their login session; you never need to ask for or pass an account ID. Call this before discussing the account.

tools.name: offer_retention
tools.description: Retention offers for a customer who wants to cancel. The billing system picks the offer; you cannot choose, change or invent one. action='quote' fetches the offer for the reason. For a price objection, first ask which features the customer cannot do without and pass them as must_keep_features: the system then looks for a cheaper plan that keeps them all. Present the offer in plain words and ask if they want it. action='accept' applies the most recently quoted offer: call it only after the customer clearly says yes, then call get_plan to verify the change before confirming it.

reason.description: Why the customer wants to cancel, in their words mapped to one code. Use 'other' only if nothing else fits.

must_keep_features.description: Features the customer said they must keep. Use only with action='quote'.

tools.name: cancel_subscription
tools.description: Cancel the signed-in customer's subscription at the end of the current billing period. Irreversible. Call only when the customer has heard a retention offer, declined it, and then explicitly confirmed they want to cancel.

reason.description: Why the customer wants to cancel, in their words mapped to one code. Use 'other' only if nothing else fits.

customer_confirmed.description: true only if the customer explicitly confirmed the cancellation in this conversation.

tools.name: escalate_to_human
tools.description: Hand the conversation to a person on the retention team. Use it when the customer asks for a human, is angry or frustrated, or wants something no other tool can do. Write a short summary for the person taking over: what the customer wants and what has been tried. After calling it, tell the customer a person will join shortly and roughly how long it takes; then stop.

summary.description: For the person taking over. Plain facts; no account IDs.

beats.label: write case note
beats.title: After the chat: the model writes a case note for the CRM
beats.text: The customer already has their confirmation. This time the model confirmed from the accept call's reply and skipped reading the account back, so the journey's verify check fails. The case note is after-call work: a summary for the support team's CRM, written from the whole transcript once the chat is over. Structured outputs make the reply match a JSON schema.

beats.label: case note JSON
beats.title: The model writes the case note
beats.text: Valid JSON, every field present. But the model wrote these values from its reading of the transcript, so any of them could still be wrong. A schema checks the shape of an answer, not whether it is true.

beats.label: fact-check case note
beats.title: Fact-check the case note before saving it
beats.text: The harness checks the three fields it can prove against facts it already holds: customer_id against the login session, and outcome and offer_presented against the customer system's own log of what happened. Free text such as summary cannot be checked this way. All three match, so the note is saved.
